dialect.detail: Standard COBOL-85 with ACCEPT FROM DATE YYYYMMDD extension; SOURCE-COMPUTER/OBJECT-COMPUTER listed as IBMPC suggesting a PC-based compiler (possibly Micro Focus or similar), but no vendor-specific extensions are visible

purpose.domain_detail: Student programming exercise involving a pizza truck inventory report with control-break logic
purpose.summary: This program reads a flat file containing records for two pizza/treat delivery trucks, processes an array of treat items per record, computes per-item revenue and per-truck totals, and writes a formatted report with headers, detail lines, truck totals, and a grand total. It uses a control-break technique to separate output by truck ID.

notable_features: OCCURS 3 TIMES array in both FILE SECTION and WORKING-STORAGE
Control-break logic between two truck IDs
PERFORM VARYING loop over array subscript
EVALUATE TRUE for size code expansion (L/M/S to LARGE/MEDIUM/SMALL)
ACCEPT FROM DATE YYYYMMDD for current date
Numeric validation with NOT NUMERIC checks
Edited PIC clauses with $ZZZ,ZZZ.99 for currency output
No COMP-3, no EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS
ORGANIZATION IS LINE SEQUENTIAL for input file
verdict.notes: Program is clearly a student assignment (AUTHOR field shows a personal name, domain is pizza trucks, comments are explanatory/tutorial in style). The file is truncated at 16000 chars but the truncation appears near the end of the PROCEDURE DIVISION; the core logic is fully visible. No vendor-specific directives present; IBMPC as computer name suggests a PC COBOL compiler environment.
